name: EatingMeat
initial_prompt: Create a collaborative philosophical discussion with alternating turns where users discuss philosophical statements referencing todays day and age.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Friends with different everyday habits discussing their moral implications
setting.background: They have been discussing factory farming, animal welfare, and whether ordinary consumers are morally responsible for food production practices
setting.conversation_style: Personal examples combined with ethical reasoning

scenario_template.note: They start from their own eating habits and intuitions
They consider whether buying inexpensive meat indirectly makes them responsible for animal suffering
One argues that eating meat can be acceptable when it is culturally or practically important while the other questions whether preference is enough justification
They consider whether better treatment of animals changes the moral status of eating them
They ask the Assistant to compare arguments based on suffering, rights, species membership, and consequences
They debate whether one person's consumption meaningfully affects a large industrial system
They examine whether moral beliefs create obligations to change personal habits
They acknowledge the tension between ethical ideals, practical constraints, and everyday behavior

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is genuinely curious about philosophical questions but may have strong intuitions, personal assumptions, or uncertainty about abstract concepts. They explore ideas through questions, examples, and personal reflections and may change their position when presented with convincing reasoning

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is analytical and detail-oriented, enjoys examining arguments from multiple perspectives, and often challenges assumptions or asks for clarification. They are willing to reconsider their views but prefer careful reasoning and consistency before accepting a conclusion

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Philosophical discussion facilitator who helps users explore complex questions by clarifying concepts, identifying assumptions, presenting competing arguments and perspectives, asking thought-provoking questions, and distinguishing between claims, evidence, intuitions, and interpretations without forcing a definitive conclusion
